newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DUVAL AND PARNEVIK SAHRE FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT PEBBLE BEACH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUVAL AND PARNEVIK SAHRE FIRST-ROUND LEAD AT PEBBLE BEACH.

text.p: David Duval and Sweden's Jesper Parnevik shared the first-round lead at the Pebble Beach National Pro-Am with rounds of seven under par 65 on Thursday.
One stroke behind at 66 were Tom Lehman and Brian Henninger, both of whom played Poppy, as well as Billy Andrade, whose 66 was shot at Spyglass Hill.
Nine players were tied at 67, including Nick Faldo, Phil Mickelson, Mark Brooks and Vijay Singh.
The tournament produced record crowds on Thursday, but few spectators were following the leaders.
The pairing of Tiger Woods and amateur partner Kevin Costner drew galleries 12 deep around every tee and green.
Woods shot a two under par 70 at Spyglass to finish in a tie for 46th, and the Woods-Costner team was at 64 to be in 29th place.

Poppy Hills is considered the easiest of the three Monterey Peninsula courses on the tournament rotation. Spyglass is the most difficult and the degree of difficulty for Pebble Beach is dependent on the weather.
"I think Billy [Andrade]'s 66 at Spygalss is a better score than my 65," Duval said.

The 180-man field of professionals, each paired with an amateur, plays the three courses in the first three rounds, with the low 60 pros and the 25 best pro-am teams playing at Pebble in the final round on Sunday.

The heavy rains that have fallen this month forced the PGA Tour to cancel practice rounds on the three courses, and play preferred lies during the tournament. Players are allowed to lift, clean and then place the golf balls within a club length on every shot that does not land on a green.

"Seeing how unbelievably wet the course was today," Faldo said, "they obviously made the right decision to allow us to tee it up everywhere. But doing that you can save as many as four shots. That may be why the scores are all so close together."
The advantage of placing the ball, as well as there being virtually no roll, provided numerous birdie opportunities. Parnevik birdied seven of his last 11 holes, and Duval seven of the last 10.

Both of the leaders came to Pebble with strong games. Parnevik had his two best finishes on the U.S. tour in the last two weeks, with a third place at the Bob Hope Classic and second palce last week at the Phoenix Open.
Duval was in second at Phoenix after three rounds, but shot a 78 on Sunday.
